title: GDE 2: Governance and school safety in Gauteng
description: SGB elections and terms, working with the GDE district office, school safety requirements, learner discipline and reporting serious incidents in Gauteng public schools.

lessons.title: SGB elections and terms
lessons.summary: When SGBs are elected, how long members serve and what a new SGB should do.
lessons.body:
## 🗳️ SGB elections in Gauteng

This module covers Gauteng public schools only. Independent schools have boards of governors set up under their own constitutions, so these rules do not apply to them.

The South African Schools Act 84 of 1996 (SASA) sets the basics. Section 31(1) says the term of office of a governing body member other than a learner may not exceed three years. Section 31(2) limits a learner member's term to one year. That is why SGB elections run nationally on a three year cycle.

### 📅 When the last elections were

The last national round of SGB elections ran in public schools from 1 to 31 March 2024, launched by the Minister of Basic Education in February 2024. Gauteng schools took part in that round. Your school's exact election date is in its own election records, so check those rather than assuming a date.

On a three year cycle, the next round is expected in 2027. The exact dates are set by notice and by GDE circular closer to the time.

> ⚠️ Watch out: Gauteng elections are run under provincial election regulations and GDE guidelines issued for each cycle under the Gauteng School Education Act 6 of 1995. We could not verify the current notice number, so we do not quote one here. Ask your district for the election regulations and circular for the coming cycle as soon as they are published.

## 👥 Who sits on the SGB

Under SASA section 23, the SGB is made up of elected members (parents, educators, non-educator staff and, in secondary schools, learners from Grade 8 up), the principal as an ex officio member, and any co-opted members. Section 23(9) requires parent members to be the majority, with one more parent than the total of the other voting members.

Learner members are chosen from the Representative Council of Learners (RCL), in line with SASA section 11 and the provincial rules.

## 🔄 Vacancies between elections

People leave: a parent's child matriculates, or a teacher resigns. A parent member whose last child leaves the school can no longer serve as a parent member. The provincial election regulations set how vacancies are filled between elections, usually by a by-election, so follow the GDE rules in force for the current term.

> 💡 Tip: keep an SGB register with each member's category, start date and contact details. When a vacancy comes up, tell the district and ask which by-election steps apply.

## 🧑‍⚖️ After the election

New SGBs should:

1. Elect office bearers, including a parent chairperson, as required by SASA section 29 (the chairperson must be a parent member who is not employed at the school).
2. Confirm or update the school's key policies: admission, language, code of conduct for learners and finance.
3. Attend the induction training the GDE offers. SASA section 19 places a duty on the HOD to build the capacity of governing bodies.
4. Make sure the district office has the new SGB's names and contact details.

### 💬 Example

At a Pretoria primary school, two parent members' children leave for high school in December 2025. The SGB secretary emails the district office in January, asks for the by-election procedure, and plans the vote before the parent majority is lost.

## ✅ Key points
- Parent and staff members serve up to three years (SASA s31(1)); learner members up to one year (SASA s31(2)).
- The last national SGB elections were held from 1 to 31 March 2024; the next round is expected in 2027.
- Parents must form the majority of the SGB (SASA s23(9)).
- Gauteng-specific election rules come from provincial regulations and GDE circulars: get the current ones from your district.

lessons.title: The district office and escalation
lessons.summary: What the district does for your school and how to escalate an issue properly.
lessons.body:
## 🏢 The district office

The Gauteng Department of Education (GDE) runs its schools through 15 education districts, each led by a District Director. For an SGB, the district office is the front door to the Department. It is where you go for:

- circulars and their deadlines
- admissions issues and placement queries (the Gauteng admission regulations give the District Director roles in objections, transfers and undocumented learners)
- governance support and SGB training
- reporting serious incidents at the school
- disputes the school cannot settle itself

Each school has an assigned official at the district who supports it. Find out who that person is and keep their details in your SGB file.

> 💡 Tip: when a new SGB starts, ask the district for a one page contact list: your support official, the governance unit, the admissions office and the safety contact.

## 🧭 How to escalate an issue

Most problems should be settled at the lowest level that can fix them. A typical route is:

1. **Inside the school.** The principal handles day to day management. SASA section 16(3) gives professional management to the principal under the HOD's authority, and section 16A sets the principal's duties, including reporting to the SGB.
2. **The SGB.** Governance issues go to the SGB at a properly called meeting. Record decisions in the minutes.
3. **The district office.** Write to the district, set out the facts, what the school has tried and what you are asking for.
4. **The Head of Department.** If the district cannot resolve it, the matter can go to the HOD, who holds the powers SASA gives the provincial department.
5. **The MEC.** Some decisions carry a right of appeal to the MEC, for example admission refusals (SASA s5(9)) and expulsions (SASA s9).

> ⚠️ Watch out: always put an escalation in writing and keep proof of delivery. Phone calls are easy to forget and hard to prove.

## 🛑 When the HOD steps in

SASA gives the HOD strong powers over SGBs:

- **Section 22** lets the HOD withdraw a function from an SGB on reasonable grounds, after giving notice and a chance to make representations.
- **Section 25** lets the HOD appoint people to perform the SGB's functions if the SGB has ceased to perform its functions.
- **Section 16(2)** requires the SGB to stand in a position of trust towards the school.

These powers are why good records matter. An SGB that can show minutes, budgets and reports is in a strong position if the district questions it.

## 📬 Writing a good escalation letter

Keep it short and factual:

- the school's name and EMIS number
- what happened, with dates
- what the school has already done
- the rule involved (for example the regulation or section)
- the decision or help you need, and by when

### 💬 Example

A Soweto high school has a burst sewer pipe that closes the toilets for a week. The principal has logged it with the district twice. The SGB chair writes to the District Director, attaches the log references and photos, explains the health risk to learners, and asks for an emergency repair date. The SGB keeps a copy in its minutes file.

## ✅ Key points
- The GDE works through 15 districts; the district office is the SGB's main contact.
- Escalate in steps: principal, SGB, district, HOD, then MEC where an appeal right exists.
- The HOD may withdraw SGB functions (SASA s22) or appoint people to perform them (SASA s25).
- Put every escalation in writing and keep proof.

lessons.title: School safety requirements
lessons.summary: The safety regulations, safety committees, visitors and the GDE safety programme.
lessons.body:
## 🛡️ The legal base for school safety

Safety rules for Gauteng public schools come mainly from national law:

- **Regulations for Safety Measures at Public Schools**, Government Notice 1040 of 12 October 2001, made under SASA section 61 and amended in 2006. Regulation 4 declares all public schools drug free and dangerous object free zones. Other regulations deal with access to school premises (regulation 5), visits by public and political office bearers (regulation 7), visits by parents (regulation 8) and emergency and fire procedures (regulation 8F).
- **SASA section 8A**, which allows the principal or a delegate to search learners and their property, and to seize dangerous objects and illegal drugs, when there is a reasonable suspicion, under the safeguards in that section.
- The **Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993**, which applies to schools as workplaces.

> ⚠️ Watch out: we summarise the topics of the safety regulations here, not their exact wording. Get the full current text from your district before you write or update your school safety policy.

## 👥 The school safety committee

The Department of Basic Education's National School Safety Framework expects every school to have a school safety committee. The GDE has said that its safety committees identify safety needs, choose interventions, involve the community and monitor progress. A typical committee includes the principal, SGB members, educators, a learner from the RCL in a secondary school, and community partners such as the local police station or community policing forum.

A safety committee should:

- do a safety audit at least once a year and after any serious incident
- keep a safety and emergency plan, including fire drills
- check access control and the visitors' register
- report to the SGB at every meeting

## 🚪 Visitors and access

Use the access rules in the safety regulations as the base for your own visitors' procedure:

1. One controlled entrance in school hours where possible.
2. Every visitor signs the register and states the purpose of the visit.
3. Visitors wear a badge and are escorted where needed.
4. Parents visiting a class make an appointment, in line with the school's policy.
5. Officials and political office bearers follow the rules for such visits in regulation 7.

> 💡 Tip: the visitors' register is often the first document asked for after an incident. Make sure it is filled in properly every day.

## 🚓 The GDE school safety programme

The GDE runs a school safety programme together with the Gauteng Department of Community Safety, SAPS and community policing forums. Features reported by the GDE include:

- **School patrollers** who help with access control and patrols. The number placed at a school depends on the programme and its funding in a given year.
- **Operation Kgutla Molao**, launched by the MEC in July 2023 after a rise in stabbings and gang violence, which included new patroller cohorts, e-panic buttons and random searches.
- Reporting of threats and incidents to SAPS and coordination meetings with police and municipalities.

Programmes like this are renamed, resized and funded differently from year to year. Ask your district what your school currently qualifies for and how to request patrollers or a police visit.

## 📝 Reporting incidents

Report a crime to SAPS at once, and report any serious incident to your district office in the way the current GDE circular requires. We could not verify a single current GDE incident reporting form, so ask your district which form and timeframe it uses.

## ✅ Key points
- GN 1040 of 2001 declares public schools drug free and dangerous object free zones (regulation 4) and governs access and visits.
- SASA s8A allows searches and seizures on reasonable suspicion, with safeguards.
- Every school should have an active safety committee that audits risks and reports to the SGB.
- Keep a proper visitors' register and access procedure.
- Report crimes to SAPS and serious incidents to the district as the current circular requires.

lessons.title: Discipline and serious incidents
lessons.summary: The code of conduct, suspension and expulsion in Gauteng, and what must be reported.
lessons.body:
## 📘 The code of conduct

Under SASA section 8, as amended by the BELA Act, the SGB must adopt a code of conduct for learners after consulting learners, parents and educators. The code must aim at a disciplined and purposeful school environment and must include a fair disciplinary process. SASA section 10 bans corporal punishment, so no code may allow it.

For Gauteng, the Department issued a notice under SASA section 9(3) on **Misconduct of Learners at Public Schools and Disciplinary Proceedings** in October 2000. It was amended by Notice 2591 of 2001 (Provincial Gazette 72 of 9 May 2001). That notice sets out how disciplinary committees work and how suspensions with a view to expulsion are handled.

> ⚠️ Watch out: this Gauteng notice is old, and SASA section 9 was amended by the BELA Act. Where the notice and the amended Act differ, the Act wins. Ask your district for the current Gauteng notice and any newer circular before you hold a hearing.

## ⚖️ Suspension and expulsion

SASA section 9 sets the national rules. In short:

- Only the SGB may suspend a learner, after a fair hearing, and only within the limits in section 9.
- Only the HOD may expel a learner from a public school, on the SGB's recommendation after a fair hearing.
- A learner or parent may appeal an expulsion to the MEC (SASA s9(4)).

The 2001 Gauteng amendments add detail:

1. A decision of the SGB's disciplinary committee is a decision of the governing body (paragraph 4(5)).
2. Where the committee suspends a learner with a view to expulsion, the principal must send the HOD the full record and the committee's report (paragraph 6(1)).
3. The HOD then must, within five days of being told of the committee's decision, expel the learner, impose a lesser sanction, suspend the sanction for at least six months, impose another competent sanction, or find the learner not guilty (paragraph 6(3)).
4. An appeal goes to the office of the MEC within 14 days of notice of the decision (paragraph 8(2)).

The notice defines "days" as weekdays, excluding weekends, public holidays and school holidays.

### 💬 Example

A Grade 10 learner brings a knife to school. The principal searches under SASA s8A, seizes the knife, hands it to SAPS and records it. The SGB's disciplinary committee holds a fair hearing with the learner and a parent present and recommends expulsion. The principal sends the full record to the HOD through the district, and the family is told of the right to appeal to the MEC.

## 🚨 Reporting serious incidents

Some incidents must be reported outside the school:

- **Crimes** such as assault with a weapon, drugs or theft: report to SAPS.
- **Abuse or deliberate neglect of a child**: section 110 of the Children's Act 38 of 2005 requires educators and other listed professionals to report it to a designated child protection organisation, the provincial social development department or a police official.
- **Sexual offences against a child**: section 54 of the Criminal Law (Sexual Offences and Related Matters) Amendment Act 32 of 2007 requires anyone who knows of one to report it to the police.
- **The district office**: report serious incidents (deaths, serious injuries, weapons, sexual offences, violence) to the district as the current GDE circular requires.

> 💡 Tip: name one person (usually the principal or a deputy) to make reports, and keep a confidential incident log with date, time, who was told and the reference number.

## ✅ Key points
- The SGB adopts the code of conduct after consultation (SASA s8); corporal punishment is banned (SASA s10).
- Gauteng's misconduct notice of 2000, amended by Notice 2591 of 2001, sets disciplinary procedure, but SASA s9 as amended by BELA prevails.
- Only the HOD may expel; appeals go to the MEC.
- Abuse must be reported under Children's Act s110; sexual offences against children under s54 of Act 32 of 2007.
- Report serious incidents to the district as the current circular requires.

questions.text: What is the maximum term of office of a parent member of a public school SGB?
questions.explanation: SASA s31(1) says the term of office of a member other than a learner may not exceed three years.

questions.text: When were the last national SGB elections held in public schools?
questions.explanation: The national SGB election window ran from 1 to 31 March 2024, in line with the three year term in SASA s31.

questions.text: Which group must form the majority of a public school SGB?
questions.explanation: SASA s23(9) requires the number of parent members to be one more than the combined total of the other voting members.

questions.text: Who may withdraw a function from an SGB on reasonable grounds?

options.text: The parent body at an AGM

questions.explanation: SASA s22 allows the HOD to withdraw an SGB function on reasonable grounds, after notice and a chance to make representations.

questions.text: An SGB cannot resolve an issue with the school's principal. What is usually the next step?

options.text: Write to the district office with the facts and what the school has tried
Post the complaint on social media
Ask the local SAPS station to decide

questions.explanation: The district office is the SGB's main contact in the GDE; issues go to the HOD and then the MEC (for example SASA s5(9) or s9) only where needed.

questions.text: What does regulation 4 of the Regulations for Safety Measures at Public Schools (GN 1040 of 2001) declare?

options.text: That schools must employ private security guards
That every school must have CCTV
That all public schools are drug free and dangerous object free zones
That parents may not visit schools

questions.explanation: Regulation 4 of GN 1040 of 2001, made under SASA s61, declares all public schools drug free and dangerous object free zones.

questions.text: Under which provision may a principal search a learner when there is a reasonable suspicion of a dangerous object or illegal drugs?

options.text: Regulation 16 of the Gauteng admission regulations

questions.explanation: SASA s8A allows the principal or a delegate to search learners and their property and seize dangerous objects and illegal drugs, with safeguards.

questions.text: Who may expel a learner from a Gauteng public school?
questions.explanation: Under SASA s9, only the HOD may expel a learner from a public school; the Gauteng notice amended by Notice 2591 of 2001 (paragraph 6(3)) sets the HOD's options.

questions.text: Under the 2001 Gauteng amendments, within what period must an appeal against an expulsion decision be delivered to the MEC's office?
questions.explanation: Paragraph 8(2) of the Gauteng misconduct notice, as amended by Notice 2591 of 2001, sets 14 days; SASA s9(4) gives the national right of appeal to the MEC.

questions.text: An educator suspects a learner is being abused at home. What does the law require?

options.text: Wait for the parent to raise it
Report it under section 110 of the Children's Act 38 of 2005
Discuss it only at the next SGB meeting
Handle it through the code of conduct

questions.explanation: Section 110 of the Children's Act 38 of 2005 requires educators to report suspected abuse to a designated child protection organisation, social development or the police.
